entry.title: Stop Using Text Diff for JSON: A Better Way to Compare Objects
entry.summary: You have two JSON objects. Maybe one is a response from your production API, and the other is from staging. You want to see if the data has changed. You paste them into a standard text diff tool, and the entire screen lights up red. Why? Because one API server serialized the keys as {"id": 1, "name": "Alice"} and the other did {"name": "Alice", "id": 1}. To a computer doing a text comparison, these strings are completely different. To a human (and your application logic), they are identical. This frustration is why I built the JSON Diff & Validator tool at Diff Guru. Here is why standard text diffs fail at JSON, and how we solved it. Standard diff algorithms (like the Myers difference algorithm) work linearly. They compare sequences of characters or lines. entry.title: Day 16.Create IAM User
entry.summary:
Lab Information
When establishing infrastructure on the AWS cloud, Identity and Access Management (IAM) is among the first and most critical services to configure. IAM facilitates the creation and management of user accounts, groups, roles, policies, and other access controls. The Nautilus DevOps team is currently in the process of configuring these resources and has outlined the following requirements: For this task, create an IAM user named iamuser_rose. Log in to AWS Console Use your provided console URL and credentials. Open IAM Service In the AWS Console search bar → type IAM Click IAM to open the Identity and Access Management dashboard. Create the IAM User On the left menu → click Users Click Create user In the User name field → enter: iamuser_rose Click Next Click Create user
